svg.text: claudia — connecting to a server and trusting its certificate, proposed (E5.8, Linux shell)

Native dialogs are Adw.AlertDialog (libadwaita 1.5, the shell's floor). They follow the system light/dark setting. Everything else stays in the web page: the Servers list and the Connect box are the page's own.
A · First connection, certificate from no known authority
Appears after Connect, only when the server answers over https with a certificate the system does not trust.
demo.example.org:8420 identifies itself with a certificate that no
certificate authority has signed. Continue only if this is your own server
or its administrator gave you the fingerprint below.
Claudia remembers this certificate for this server only,
and warns you if it ever changes.
Esc and the default button (focused first) are Cancel. If the certificate was issued for another name,
an amber line “Issued for another address” is added under “Issued by”.
B · The trusted certificate has changed
Same address, different certificate than the one you trusted. Stronger wording; Cancel stays the default.
demo.example.org:8420 now shows a different certificate from the one
you trusted on 10 Nov 2026. Someone may be intercepting your connection,
or the administrator may have renewed it. Ask them before you go on.
Not offered when the new certificate has expired.
The second button is Adwaita’s destructive style. There is no “always trust” and no “ignore once”.
C · When Connect cannot go through
The page’s own error line under the address field (the one that says “Type a server address.” today).
Use https:// — plain http is only allowed for this computer.
That server runs Claudia Composes. This window is Claudia Computes — open it there.
The certificate of old.example.org has expired. Ask its administrator to renew it.
That does not look like a Claudia server.
Not connected: you did not trust this server’s certificate.
Cases 1–5 never reach the trust dialog; 6 follows Cancel in A or B. Messages are translatable like the rest.
D · What happens after Connect, in this order
The same for a typed address and for a click in the Servers list. The first failing step stops it.
https, or http only for this computer
the server’s app equals this window’s
this window now shows that server
After 4, the address is saved in this app’s own server list (never a password or secret).
“This computer” stays in the list and always means this window’s own local server.
· Forgetting a trusted certificate: proposed as “Remove” on a server in the list (which also
forgets its certificate). The list has no remove action yet, so it is not drawn here.
· An expired or not-yet-valid certificate is never offered for trust (message 4).
